page: Vultr vhp-2c-2gb-amd is an entry-level virtual server within the High Performance product line, powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The instance provisions 2 shared vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory and 60 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU package features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AES, and SHA-NI. The configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not include GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread execution alongside constraints typical of shared-core architectures. The server achieves a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3206.39, while multi-core stress-ng throughput remains in the median range at 6339.69. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show 41.62 GB/sec read and 33.03 GB/sec write throughput. In contrast, memory-intensive metrics reflect lower placement, including a PassMark memory score of 1240.01 and static web serving throughput of 2.53 GB/sec, illustrating bottlenecks imposed by the 2.0 GB memory footprint.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1.0 GB memory-per-core ratio and shared CPU allocation represent a cost-effective design tailored for lightweight compute requirements rather than heavy concurrent execution. The bundled 60 GB NVMe SSD provides fast local I/O compared to standard virtual disks. The platform is well-matched for development environments, task workers, single-threaded batch scripts, microservices, and low-traffic web serving where memory demands remain strictly limited.
description: Vultr vhp-2c-2gb-amd is an entry-level virtual server in the High Performance lineup, powered by a shared AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The instance provisions 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 2.0 GB of RAM, and 60 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, along with one complimentary public IPv4 address and no GPU acceleration. In synthetic benchmarks, the server registers top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng tests, supported by average multi-core compute and standard uncached memory bandwidth. However, the lean 1.0 GB per-core memory allocation and shared compute resources constrain high-concurrency database operations and high-throughput static web serving. Delivering an economical hardware footprint with fast local storage, this instance is best aligned with lightweight background workers, basic automation tasks, microservices, and low-traffic utility web applications.
